source.title: Tame topology of arithmetic quotients and algebraicity of Hodge loci
source.authors: Benjamin Bakker, Bruno Klingler, Jacob Tsimerman
source.venue: Journal of the American Mathematical Society 33 (2020), 917–939
readSections: Complete published original, printed pp.917–939: §§1–5, Appendix A, acknowledgements and references.
Published images pp.921,923,926–928,930–933,935 inspected for formula and symbol verification.
Complete four-page official erratum reread; author copy compared at the main statements and recorded findings.
Earlier contributors read the complete author copy and selected prerequisite papers to the exact extents in provenance.
source.version: Typeset published original, read completely, with official JAMS 36 (2023) erratum (DOI 10.1090/jams/1025). Author copy compared at main statements and every recorded finding; no claim of exhaustive glyph-by-glyph collation.

summary: Bakker–Klingler–Tsimerman show that arithmetic quotients carry a natural R_alg-definable structure, that period maps of polarized integral variations of Hodge structure are R_an,exp-definable (Theorem 1.3), and deduce, with the definable Chow theorem, that the components of the Hodge locus are algebraic (Theorem 1.6), a new proof of Cattani–Deligne–Kaplan. Reviewed by REV-PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 147 items (10 library, 14 planned, 123 missing). 60 mistakes are recorded (34 misprints, 16 gaps, 10 errors; 4 reach a stated result, 16 a proof). The 2023 erratum corrects Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.5; with it, Theorems 1.3 and 1.6 stand. Not formalised.

items.name: Existing pure Hodge structure
items.statement: On a complex vector space W with conjugation ω, a weight-k pure Hodge structure is an exhaustive decreasing filtration F with F^p complementary to the conjugate of F^(k+1−p). The integral specialization uses a lattice and its complexification.

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.pieceDecomposition
api.statement: Recover F^a as the direct sum of H^(p,k−p) with p≥a.

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.conjugatePiece
api.statement: Conjugation sends H^(p,k−p) to H^(k−p,p).

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.shiftWeight
api.statement: A Tate shift by m has weight k−2m and filtration F^(p+m).

uses.how: Specify fibrewise opposed filtrations with the same weight.

unitTests.name: BKT.PureHodge.test3

items.name: Existing module-valued local system
items.statement: An R-module local coefficient system on a topological space X is a functor from its fundamental groupoid to ModuleCat R. For the integral PVHS consumer the fibres must additionally be finite free Z-modules; the generic carrier alone imposes neither freeness nor finiteness.

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.transportCompose
api.statement: Transport along a concatenation is the composite in the selected path convention.

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.finiteFreeFibres
api.statement: A PVHS adapter explicitly requires each integral fibre finite free; this is additional to LocalCoefficientSystem.

uses.how: Supply flat integral fibres and monodromy transport.

unitTests.name: BKT.LocalSystem.test3

items.name: Existing polarized period-domain point
items.statement: Fix a finite free Z-lattice V, its complexification, integral bilinear form Q, weight k and a finite-support symmetric Hodge type. A point is a Hodge filtration of that type polarized by Q. This carrier does not provide topology or a complex manifold.

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.filtrationExt

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.hodgeRanks

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.fixedPolarization
api.statement: The same input integral form polarizes every point; changing the form changes the parameter, not a field of the point.

items.name: Existing Weil operator
items.statement: For a weight-k pure Hodge structure, C is the complex-linear endomorphism acting by i^(p−q) on H^(p,q), where p+q=k.

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.onPiece

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.square
api.statement: C²=(−1)^k times the identity in weight k.

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.realCompatibility
api.statement: C commutes with conjugation on the real form.

items.name: Existing Hermitian Hodge form
items.statement: For a polarization Q, the pinned library form is h_lib(u,v) = Q(C(conj u), v), conjugate-linear in u and linear in v. It is the complex conjugate of the form the paper means, h_BKT(u,v) = Q_C(C u, conj v); this is the form behind (4.4) and B(u,v) := Q_C(u, conj v). The printed definition on p. 930 reads h_z(u,v) := Q_C(C_z u, v) with no conjugation, which is a misprint (new sourceIssue). The diagonal real norms agree.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.conventionConjugate
api.statement: h_lib(u,v)=conj(h_BKT(u,v)) with the displayed Weil and polarization conventions.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.diagonalAgreement
api.statement: h_lib(u,u)=h_BKT(u,u) is real.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.sesquilinearity
api.statement: h_lib(au,bv)=conj(a)b h_lib(u,v).

uses.how: Use diagonal norms while reconciling conjugation conventions.

unitTests.name: BKT.HodgeForm.test2

unitTests.name: BKT.HodgeForm.test3

items.name: Existing positivity of the Hodge form
items.statement: For any polarization P and nonzero vector u in the complexification, P.hodgeForm(u,u)>0. In particular its real restriction is positive definite. Nonzero u is essential.
proofSteps: Import the pinned positivity theorem; convert the sesquilinear convention using hodge-form.

items.name: Existing rational mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: On compatible rational and complex models of an integral module, a mixed Hodge structure consists of a finite increasing rational weight filtration W and finite decreasing complex Hodge filtration F for which gr^W_k with its induced F is pure of weight k.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.gradedPure
api.statement: The k-th rational weight graded with its induced F is pure of weight k.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.rationalWeight

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.pureAsMixed
api.statement: A pure weight-k structure defines a mixed structure with only gr_k nonzero.

uses.how: Package the shifted monodromy filtration and limiting F.

items.name: Existing Deligne bigrading
items.statement: For a mixed Hodge structure, I^(p,q)=(F^p∩W_(p+q))∩((conj F^q∩W_(p+q))+Σ_(j≥2)(conj F^(q−j+1)∩W_(p+q−j))). The weights here use the actual mixed weight; centered monodromy indices require a shift by the pure weight.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.recoverF
api.statement: F^a is the sum of I^(p,q) for p≥a.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.recoverW
api.statement: W_k is the sum of I^(p,q) for p+q≤k.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.conjugateModuloLower
api.statement: conj I^(p,q) equals I^(q,p) modulo pieces with first index<q and second index<p.

uses.how: Import the one-filtration decomposition without assuming the multi-filtration extension.

items.name: Existing direct-sum and filtration recovery
items.statement: The I^(p,q) form an internal direct sum of the underlying complex vector space. F^p∩W_k is the sum of the pieces I^(r,s) with r≥p and r+s≤k. This concerns one mixed Hodge structure, not simultaneous splittings of several monodromy filtrations.
proofSteps: Use the pinned internal direct sum and simultaneous F/W truncation theorem.

items.name: Existing finite exponential of a nilpotent
items.statement: For a nilpotent a in a Q-algebra with a^m=0, exp_nil(a)=Σ_(0≤j<m) a^j/j!. Commuting nilpotents a,b satisfy exp_nil(a+b)=exp_nil(a)exp_nil(b). The analytic exponential comparison is a separate interface if needed.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.truncate
api.statement: If N^m=0, exp_nil(zN)=Σ_(j<m) z^j N^j/j!.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.commutingSum
api.statement: For commuting nilpotents A,B, exp_nil(A+B)=exp_nil(A)exp_nil(B).

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.inverse
api.statement: exp_nil(N)exp_nil(−N)=1.

uses.how: Use a finite algebraic polynomial for monodromy twists.

items.name: Expansions of the ordered real field
items.statement: A structure S on R expanding the real field is a collection (S_n)_{n≥1}, where S_n is a set of subsets of R^n (the S-definable sets), such that: all algebraic subsets of R^n are in S_n; S_n is a Boolean subalgebra of the power set of R^n; if A ∈ S_n and B ∈ S_m then A × B ∈ S_{n+m}; if p: R^{n+1} → R^n is a linear projection and A ∈ S_{n+1} then p(A) ∈ S_n. A function f: A → B between S-definable sets is S-definable if its graph is S-definable.

items.name: O-minimality
items.statement: An expansion of the ordered real field is o-minimal if every definable subset of R is a finite union of points and intervals.

items.name: Restricted analytic functions
items.statement: A function f: R^n → R is restricted analytic if it is zero outside [0,1]^n and coincides on [0,1]^n with a real analytic function g defined on a neighbourhood of [0,1]^n. (Consequence not stated in the paper but used in Lemma 4.2 and Definition 4.4: a function analytic on a neighbourhood of any compact box or closed polydisk, restricted to it, is R_an-definable, because semialgebraic rescaling and finite covering by boxes reduce it to [0,1]^n.)
items.locator: §1.2, p. 919; used in Lemma 4.2 and Definition 4.4 (ring O of restricted analytic functions on Δ^n), p. 929

api.name: BKT.RestrictedAnalytic.complexComponents

uses.how: Restrict trigonometric functions and the untwisted period map on buffered compact boxes.

items.name: The structures R_alg, R_an, R_exp and R_an,exp
items.statement: R_alg is the structure whose definable sets are the semi-algebraic sets. R_an := ⟨R, +, ×, <, {f} for f restricted analytic⟩ is generated from R_alg by adding the restricted analytic functions. R_exp := ⟨R, +, ×, <, exp: R → R⟩ is generated from R_alg by making the real exponential definable. R_an,exp := ⟨R, +, ×, <, exp, {f} for f restricted analytic⟩ is generated by R_an and R_exp. Hence R_alg ⊂ R_an, R_exp ⊂ R_an,exp, and a set or map definable in a smaller structure is definable in a larger one.

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.algebraicToAnalytic
api.statement: R_alg-definable sets are R_an-definable.

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.analyticToCombined
api.statement: R_an-definability implies R_an,exp-definability.

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.realExpDefinable

items.name: O-minimality of the required real expansions
items.statement: R_alg, R_an, R_exp and R_an,exp are o-minimal. The R_an case uses Gabrielov/van den Dries and the combined case uses van den Dries–Miller; the combined assertion is not inferred merely from o-minimality of its two reducts.
proofSteps: Import the individual original theorems with their languages; their proofs remain source-audit leaves.

items.name: Definable manifolds with finite atlas
items.statement: A paracompact Hausdorff space has a definable manifold structure if it has a finite cover by coordinate neighborhoods with definable chart images, overlaps and transition homeomorphisms. Structures are identified when mixed transitions are definable.

items.name: Definable images, pullbacks and finite gluing
items.statement: Graphs of maps between finite definable atlases define maps independently of the atlas. Composition, finite products, images and inverse images are definable; maps that agree on a finite definable cover glue definably. Descent through a definable surjection holds by projecting the graph of the composite.
items.locator: Implicit; App. A.2, p. 935 defines only definable subsets and definable maps (by graphs). The calculus (images, preimages, composition, gluing) is used without statement in §4.6, p. 933 and §5, pp. 933–934 (Y as an image of a definable map, W = Φ_S^{-1}(Y)); standard background [VDD98, Ch. 10]
proofSteps: Translate each claim into finite Boolean operations and coordinate projection.
For descent, existentially quantify a source representative; constancy on fibres supplies a well-defined graph.

items.name: Real analytic manifolds with corners
items.statement: Let X be a paracompact Hausdorff space and n ≥ 1. An n-dimensional chart with corners is a pair (U, φ) with U open in R^n_k := R^k_{≥0} × R^{n−k} for some 0 ≤ k ≤ n, and φ : U → X a homeomorphism onto a non-empty open set φ(U). A continuous α : A → B (A ⊂ R^m, B ⊂ R^n) is real analytic if it extends to a real analytic map between open neighbourhoods of A and B. Two charts (U, φ), (V, ψ) are real analytically compatible if ψ^{-1}∘φ : φ^{-1}(φ(U)∩ψ(V)) → ψ^{-1}(φ(U)∩ψ(V)) is a homeomorphism and it and its inverse are real analytic in this sense. An atlas is a family of pairwise compatible charts covering X; every atlas lies in a unique maximal atlas. A real analytic manifold with corners of dimension n is X with a maximal n-dimensional real analytic atlas with corners. Weakly real analytic maps are the continuous maps that are real analytic in charts ([Joy12, def. 3.1]).

items.name: Definable manifolds with corners
items.statement: Let ℛ be a fixed o-minimal expansion of R and X a paracompact Hausdorff space. An n-dimensional chart with corners (U, φ) is ℛ-definable if U is an ℛ-definable subset of R^n (equivalently of R^n_k). Two ℛ-definable charts are ℛ-compatible if ψ^{-1}∘φ is an ℛ-definable homeomorphism between the ℛ-definable sets φ^{-1}(φ(U)∩ψ(V)) and ψ^{-1}(φ(U)∩ψ(V)). An ℛ-definable atlas with corners is a finite family of pairwise ℛ-compatible ℛ-definable charts covering X. Two atlases are ℛ-equivalent if all mixed transition maps (ψ_j^{-1}∘φ_i; printed ψ_j∘φ_i^{-1}, E25) are ℛ-definable. An ℛ-definable manifold with corners of dimension n is X with an ℛ-equivalence class of such atlases. Z ⊂ X is ℛ-definable (open, closed) if every φ_i^{-1}(Z ∩ φ_i(U_i)) is ℛ-definable (open, closed) in U_i. A map is ℛ-definable if its graph is ℛ-definable in the product manifold (with corners).

items.name: Compact analytic corners admit a canonical R_an structure
items.statement: Proposition A.2 (first assertion). Let X be a compact real analytic n-manifold with corners. Then X has a natural structure of an R_an-definable manifold with corners. It is the structure given by a finite atlas of real analytic charts (U_i, φ_i) whose domains U_i ⊂ R^n_k are relatively compact and semi-analytic, and the proof asserts that it is independent of the finite subfamily and of the choice of the U_i.
proofSteps: For every point choose a corner chart and a smaller relatively open semialgebraic box with compact closure inside the original chart domain. Its image is a neighborhood; use compactness to select finitely many such neighborhoods.
Apply buffered-transition-graph to every pair of the selected charts. This verifies both definable overlaps and definable transitions, not merely analyticity on open overlaps.
For two choices of buffered covers, apply the same graph lemma to all mixed pairs. The identity is definable, proving independence.
Apply the construction to local boundary branches to obtain the canonical finite boundary atlas and its definable immersion.
items.note: Compatibility is asserted for buffered finite analytic subatlases; an arbitrary nonbuffered analytic chart need not be globally subanalytic. SourceIssues E17 records the missing buffer in the printed argument. The printed proof needs smaller corner boxes whose closures lie in larger analytic charts (E17); the repair shows that the matching graph of two such charts is a compact definable set: Let φ_i:U_i→X and φ_j:U_j→X be compatible real analytic corner charts. Let B_i⊂U_i and B_j⊂U_j be relatively open semialgebraic boxes whose closures are compact subsets of the respective original chart domains. Then the graph of φ_j⁻¹φ_i on B_i∩φ_i⁻¹(φ_j(B_j)) is globally subanalytic, hence R_an-definable.

items.name: Definability of boundary immersion and interior
items.statement: For compact analytic X with corners and its canonical R_an structure, the boundary-branch immersion i_X is R_an-definable, and X minus its image is a definable manifold.
proofSteps: Apply the same finite buffered atlas construction to the compact boundary.
Locally the immersion inserts a zero coordinate, so its graph is definable; take its image and complement.

items.name: Rational parabolic and horospherical data
items.statement: Let 𝐏 be a ℚ-parabolic subgroup of 𝐆, 𝐍_P its unipotent radical, 𝐋_P = 𝐍_P\𝐏 its Levi quotient, and N_P, P, L_P their groups of real points. Let 𝐒_P be the (ℚ-)split centre of 𝐋_P, A_P the identity component of 𝐒_P(ℝ), 𝐌_P := ⋂_{χ∈X*(𝐋_P)} ker χ² (ℚ-characters) and M_P = 𝐌_P(ℝ); then L_P = A_P M_P. A point x of the symmetric space X (maximal compact K_x, Cartan involution θ_x) determines a unique θ_x-stable real Levi subgroup 𝐋_{P,x} ⊂ 𝐏_ℝ lifting (𝐋_P)_ℝ [BS73, 1.9], not necessarily defined over ℚ; lifting A_P, M_P into it gives P = N_P A_{P,x} M_{P_x} (2.1) and the horospherical decomposition G = N_P A_{P,x} M_{P_x} K_x (2.2), i.e. the multiplication map N_P × A_P × (M_P K) → G is a (semi-algebraic, real analytic) diffeomorphism (used on p. 925). In these coordinates p₀ = n₀a₀m₀ ∈ P acts by left multiplication: (n₀a₀m₀)(n,a,m) = (n₀·(a₀m₀)n(a₀m₀)⁻¹, a₀a, m₀m) (2.3) [BJ06a, Lemma 2.3] (printed as a 'right action', see E10).

items.name: Positive root coordinates and truncations
items.statement: Let Φ(A_P,N_P) be the set of characters of A_P on the Lie algebra 𝔫_P ('the roots of P with respect to A_P'); a ↦ a^α is semi-algebraic. There is a unique subset Δ(A_P,N_P) = {α₁,…,α_r} of Φ(A_P,N_P) consisting of dim A_P linearly independent roots such that every root is a combination of them with non-negative integral coefficients (the simple roots; the paper writes 'positive'). For t > 0, A_{P,t} := {a ∈ A_P : a^α > t for all α ∈ Δ(A_P,N_P)}. The map e_P : A_P → (ℝ_{>0})^r, e_P(a) = (a^{−α₁},…,a^{−α_r}) (2.4), is a semi-algebraic diffeomorphism; \bar{A_P} := [0,∞)^r is the closure of e_P(A_P) in ℝ^r and \bar{A_{P,t}} ⊂ \bar{A_P} is the closure of e_P(A_{P,t}) (that is, [0,1/t]^r).
items.locator: §2.2, pp. 923–924 (roots, simple roots, Definition 2.3); §2.3, p. 925, equation (2.4) and the closures \bar{A_P}, \bar{A_{P,t}}

items.name: Semialgebraic Siegel set for fixed K
items.statement: (Definition 2.3, p. 924) For a ℚ-parabolic 𝐏, a maximal compact K = K_x (with the θ_x-stable Levi data of 𝐏), t > 0 and bounded U ⊂ N_P, W ⊂ M_P K, the set 𝔖 := U × A_{P,t} × W ⊂ G (horospherical coordinates) is a Siegel set for G associated to 𝐏 and K; it is semi-algebraic when U and W are relatively compact open semi-algebraic subsets, and only such Siegel sets are used. (Definition 2.5 as corrected by the erratum, §1.1, p. 1) For a fixed maximal compact K ⊃ M, a Siegel set for G/M associated to K is the image π(𝔖) ⊂ G/M of a Siegel set 𝔖 of G associated to 𝐏 and K for some ℚ-parabolic 𝐏; it is semi-algebraic (Remark 2.6(2)). (Erratum §1.2 uses the sets U a A_{>0} W, a ∈ A_P, U ⊂ N_P, W ⊂ M_P K bounded semi-algebraic; each set of either kind is contained in one of the other kind.)

items.name: Translation and conjugation rules with compact data
items.statement: (Lemma 2.4) If 𝔖 is a Siegel set for G associated to 𝐏 and x, then for g ∈ 𝐆(ℚ) (needed for g𝐏g⁻¹ to be rational) g𝔖g⁻¹ is a Siegel set associated to g𝐏g⁻¹ and gx (maximal compact gK_xg⁻¹). (Erratum Remark 1.1(1)) For g ∈ G, 𝔖g is a Siegel set associated to 𝐏 and g⁻¹Kg (since G = K𝐏(ℝ)); for g ∈ 𝐏(ℝ), g𝔖 is a Siegel set associated to 𝐏 and K. These are exact for the erratum §1.2 sets U a A_{>0} W; with Definition 2.3's A_{P,t} they hold with 'is contained in a Siegel set'. Consequently (Remark 2.6(1), corrected) for γ ∈ 𝐆(ℚ)⁺, γ𝔖 is contained in a Siegel set associated to γ𝐏γ⁻¹ and the same K.
items.locator: Lemma 2.4 and Remark 2.6(1), p. 924; erratum Remark 1.1(1), p. 2
proofSteps: Use the parabolic horospherical decomposition and conjugation of the Cartan involution.
Distinguish right translation, conjugation, and rational left translation; no independence of K follows.

items.name: Finite arithmetic cover by fixed-K Siegel sets
items.statement: (Proposition 2.7(1) [BJ06a, Prop. 2.5], with all Siegel sets associated to the fixed K as the erratum requires) There are only finitely many Γ-conjugacy classes of ℚ-parabolic subgroups. If 𝐏₁,…,𝐏_k represent them, there exist Siegel sets 𝔖_i = U_i × A_{P_i,t_i} × W_i associated to 𝐏_i and K (1 ≤ i ≤ k) whose images in Γ\G/M cover it.
proofSteps: Use the rational reduction theorem with fixed compact data and project the finite cover to G/M.

items.name: Finite arithmetic overlaps of Siegel sets
items.statement: For any two Siegel sets S₁,S₂ associated to the same K, the set of γ∈Γ with γS₁∩S₂ nonempty is finite. The property extends to relatively compact closures of their unipotent and Levi factors.
proofSteps: Apply the rational Siegel property, also for the enlarged compact factors.

items.name: Separation of inequivalent cusps
items.statement: If P₁ and P₂ are not Γ-conjugate, then for fixed bounded U_i,W_i and sufficiently large truncation parameters t_i, γS₁∩S₂ is empty for every γ∈Γ. All Siegel data use one K.
proofSteps: Use the cusp separation part of rational reduction theory.

items.name: Deep self-intersections come from the parabolic
items.statement: For fixed U,W and sufficiently large t, a Siegel set S for P and K satisfies γS∩S=∅ whenever γ∈Γ\(Γ∩P).
proofSteps: Apply parabolic separation to the deep positive chamber.

items.name: Deep corners for distinct parabolics separate
items.statement: For distinct rational parabolics P₁≠P₂ and fixed bounded factors using one K, the corresponding Siegel sets are disjoint once both truncation parameters are sufficiently large.
proofSteps: Use the final separation assertion of the fixed-K reduction theorem.

items.name: Semialgebraic model of G/M
items.statement: For G as above and connected compact M, the homogeneous space G/M admits a semialgebraic model inducing its quotient topology, with semialgebraic projection G→G/M and semialgebraic left G-action. Its construction is independent of the later choice of K.
proofSteps: Use E={(g,gm):g∈G,m∈M} as a semialgebraic relation in G×G. Compactness of M makes the coordinate projections proper.
Apply the exact proper semialgebraic quotient theorem to obtain the quotient topology and projection; multiplication descends to the semialgebraic left action.

Do not follow the first printed proof's composition with M-invariant polynomials on the representation: it may collapse distinct right cosets (E8). The second proof remains the planned route, with the external quotient theorem retained as a source gap.
items.note: Corrected E8 and E9. The orbit map itself separates right cosets; subsequently taking invariants for the left M-action destroys this separation.

items.name: Semialgebraic quotient of a definably proper equivalence relation
items.statement: (van den Dries, Tame topology, Ch. 10, (2.13)–(2.15), p. 166) Let X be a locally closed definable set and E ⊂ X × X a definable equivalence relation that is definably proper over X, i.e. the projection E → X, (x,y) ↦ x, is definably proper. Then a definably proper quotient p : X → X/E exists: a definable, continuous, surjective, definably proper map whose fibres are the E-classes; it is definably identifying, so X/E is homeomorphic to the topological quotient. Over ℝ_alg all data are semi-algebraic. Used for G/M in Lemma 2.1 (via [VDD98, (2.18), p. 167]) and for (∐cl(𝔖_i))/∼_E in §3.1.
proofSteps: Read and instantiate the exact definably proper quotient theorem.
Separate existence of a definable topological quotient from a finite atlas of local manifold slices.
items.note: The source theorem and its exact properness convention need original-book audit; this is an explicit open interface, not a claimed general quotient theorem without those hypotheses.

items.name: Borel–Serre corner for a rational parabolic
items.statement: For fixed K and rational P, form N_P×[0,∞)^Δ×M_PK using inverse-simple-root coordinates. Its interior is the corresponding horospherical model of G, and its zero coordinate faces record larger parabolics via their incidence relations.

items.name: Borel–Serre partial compactification for fixed K
items.statement: Fix K. The Borel–Serre partial compactification is Ḡ^BS = G ∪ ∐_𝐏 (N_P × (M_P K)), 𝐏 running over the proper ℚ-parabolics [BJ06a, §3.2]. Topology: an unbounded sequence y_j = (n_j,a_j,m_j) ∈ N_P × A_P × (M_P K) = G converges to (n,m) ∈ N_P × (M_P K) iff (a_j)^α → +∞ for every α ∈ Φ(A_P,N_P), n_j → n in N_P and m_j → m in M_P K. For 𝐏 ⊂ 𝐐 the faces are glued as in [BJ06a, pp. 274–275]. Ḡ^BS is a real analytic manifold with corners [BJ06a, Prop. 6.3]. Topology and analytic structure depend on K (erratum §1.1), but for M = K the compactification Γ\Ḡ^BS/K does not depend on K (erratum, footnote 1).
proofSteps: Use the explicit corner embeddings and parabolic incidence maps.
Audit transition maps in Borel–Ji: they are analytic, not asserted semialgebraic.

items.name: Extended commuting arithmetic and compact actions

items.name: Compact analytic corner quotient
items.statement: For neat arithmetic Γ and connected compact M⊂K, the Γ×M action gives a free proper quotient Γ\Gbar^BS_K/M, a compact real analytic manifold with corners whose interior is Γ\G/M. General torsion-free interior statements are separated from neat boundary inputs.
proofSteps: Use fixed-K reduction theory for compactness and cusp-local properness.
Use the source’s neat-level freeness statement and quotient corner charts.

items.name: Finite relation on Siegel closures

proofSteps: Represent each overlap by its finite collection of semialgebraic action graphs.
Use finite-siegel-relation-proper for the closed tagged pieces; apply the exact quotient theorem only after its external contract has been checked.

items.name: Definable structure on an arithmetic quotient with K
items.statement: For every torsion-free arithmetic Γ and connected compact M⊂K as above, Γ\G/M has an R_alg-definable manifold structure characterized by definability of π restricted to every semialgebraic Siegel set associated to K. A finite union of such sets is a semialgebraic fundamental set on which π is definable.
proofSteps: Take the definably proper finite relation quotient, then refine local slices to a finite atlas.
Enlarge a covering Siegel set to contain a rational translate of any further fixed-K Siegel set.
Use finite overlap to compare different covering choices.

items.name: Compatibility with the analytic Borel–Serre structure
items.statement: At neat level and for the same K on both constructions, the R_an expansion of arithmetic-definable-structure equals the structure induced on the interior of Γ\Gbar^BS_K/M by its compact real analytic corner atlas.
proofSteps: The inverse-root corner coordinate change is semialgebraic.
On finitely many buffered compact charts the quotient corner maps are restricted analytic.
Compare the resulting atlases; no semialgebraic assertion for every boundary transition is made.

items.name: Corrected containment of subgroup Siegel sets
items.statement: Let 𝐆 ⊃ 𝐇 be reductive ℚ-groups and 𝔖_H ⊂ 𝐇(ℝ) a Siegel set with respect to a Siegel triple (𝐏_H, 𝐒_H, K_H). In Orr's convention 𝐏_H is a minimal ℚ-parabolic, 𝐒_H is the unique ℝ-torus in 𝐏_H that is 𝐏_H(ℝ)-conjugate to a maximal ℚ-split torus and stable under the Cartan involution of K_H, and 𝔖_H = Ω A_t K_H. Let K_G ⊂ 𝐆(ℝ) be a maximal compact subgroup with (i) K_H ⊂ K_G and (ii) the Cartan involution of 𝐆 associated with K_G stabilises 𝐒_H. Then there are 𝐏_G, 𝐒_G forming a Siegel triple (𝐏_G, 𝐒_G, K_G), a Siegel set 𝔖_G with respect to it and a finite C ⊂ 𝐆(ℚ) with 𝔖_H ⊂ C·𝔖_G. Moreover R_u(𝐏_H) ⊂ R_u(𝐏_G) and 𝐒_H = 𝐒_G ∩ 𝐇.
items.locator: Orr–Schnell2023 Theorem1; replacing the fixed-K use of originalTheorem3.2
proofSteps: Use the corrected Cartan-stable torus condition in Orr’s Lemma4.4.
Then apply the remaining original reduction proof with the additional minor corrections from Orr–Schnell§E.
The correction proof is read; the full original Orr proof remains a gap.

items.name: Subgroup stability is a sufficient stronger condition
items.statement: In the setting of Orr–Schnell Theorem 1 with K_H ⊂ K_G: if the Cartan involution Θ of 𝐆 associated with K_G stabilises 𝐇 (condition (ii′)), then Θ|_𝐇 is the Cartan involution of 𝐇 associated with K_H, so Θ stabilises the torus 𝐒_H of every Siegel triple (𝐏_H,𝐒_H,K_H) (condition (ii)) and Theorem 1 applies. The converse fails: 𝐆 = SL₂, 𝐇 = {(a, db; b, a) : a² − db² = 1} with d a positive non-square rational, K_G = SO₂(ℝ), 𝐒_H = {1}. The erratum (proof of Theorem 1.2(2), p. 3) uses (ii′) in Lie-algebra form: θ_{K_G} stabilises φ(𝔤′) ⊂ 𝔤.
proofSteps: Restrict the Cartan involution and use uniqueness of the Cartan-stable split torus in the chosen minimal parabolic.

items.name: Rational Siegel intersection with a subgroup
items.statement: Let H⊂G be reductive over Q, K_H=K_G∩H(R) maximal compact, and assume every K_H-Siegel set lies in finitely many G(Q)-translates of some K_G-Siegel set. For every K_G-Siegel set S_G there are a K_H-Siegel set S_H and finite F⊂H(Q) with S_G∩H(R)⊂F S_H.
proofSteps: Choose Γ_H=Γ_G∩H and a finite rational-cusp cover H(R)=Γ_H C_H S_H.
Enlarge S_G after rationally aligning the minimal parabolics so the assumed forward containment is S_H⊂A S_G for finite rational A.
The Siegel property bounds the γ with S_G∩γ C_H A S_G nonempty. Those finitely many γC_H give F.
items.note: The forward containment hypothesis is part of the statement. Borel–Harish-Chandra7.5 for real Siegel domains is not substituted here.

items.name: Definability of compatible arithmetic morphisms
items.statement: Every compatible-morphism is R_alg-definable between the fixed-K arithmetic quotient structures.
proofSteps: Right-translate using the corresponding change of maximal compact, retaining the rational group map.
Factor the rational map through its image and establish the surjection/quotient adapter.
Apply corrected finite Siegel containment to the inclusion and descend on finite quotient atlases.
items.note: The original §3.2 product equality for arithmetic quotients needs finite-index and compact-stabilizer bookkeeping; it is not adopted literally.

items.name: Arithmetic Hecke correspondence
items.statement: For g∈Gbold(Q)∩G, the commensurable groups Γ and g⁻¹Γg have finite-index intersection. The correspondence from Γ\G/M through this intersection is given by the natural projection and left multiplication by g followed by projection.

items.name: Semialgebraicity of Hecke correspondences
items.statement: The two maps of hecke-correspondence are finite local covering maps and R_alg-definable for the chosen arithmetic quotient structure. The conjugation morphism (Int(g),g) satisfies the corrected compact compatibility.
proofSteps: Use arithmetic commensurability for finite index.
Check the compact and Cartan conditions for (Int(g),g), then apply compatible-morphism-definable.

items.name: Dependence on maximal compact is real
items.statement: Let 𝐆 = SL₂, Γ = SL₂(ℤ), 𝐏 the upper triangular subgroup and M = {1}. For x ≠ y in ℍ, a Siegel set B_N B_A K_x is not contained in any finite union of Siegel sets γB′_N B′_A K_y (γ ∈ 𝐆(ℚ)): otherwise B_N B_A K_x K_y would be, but its image B_N B_A K_x·y ⊂ ℍ has unbounded real part at unbounded height. Hence the fibre product over Γ\G of a K_x-Siegel set and a K_y-Siegel set has infinitely many connected components, so the structures S_{Γ,G,{1},K_x} and S_{Γ,G,{1},K_y} on Γ\G differ.
proofSteps: Reduce to K_y fixing i in the upper half-plane.
K_x i is a nontrivial circle; positive diagonal scaling produces unbounded horizontal coordinate, incompatible with finite K_y-Siegel coverage.
Use the resulting infinite overlap components as the definability obstruction.

items.name: Compact inclusion alone does not imply Siegel containment
items.statement: There are reductive, and also semisimple, rational subgroup inclusions with K_H⊂K_G for which an H-Siegel set is not covered by finitely many rational translates of K_G-Siegel sets. Therefore the Cartan compatibility cannot be deleted from the definable-morphism interface.
proofSteps: For the conjugate split torus in SL₂, its orbit in H is the diagonal ray (1−y)+iy, escaping all finite rational cusp-strip covers.
The SL₃ conjugate orthogonal example gives the semisimple obstruction: fixed compact subgroup but a conjugating matrix with non-diagonal ηᵗη.
Use the source’s parabolic-intersection lemma for the latter contradiction.

items.name: Polarized integral variation of Hodge structure
items.statement: A pure weight-k polarized integral variation on a complex manifold S consists of: a local system V of finitely generated Z-modules (the paper takes the fibre 'modulo torsion', §4.2 p. 928, so one may pass to the torsion-free quotient); the holomorphic bundle V⊗O_S with its flat connection; a holomorphic decreasing filtration F inducing a pure weight-k Hodge structure on each fibre; a flat (−1)^k-symmetric form Q: V⊗V → Z polarizing each fibre (Hodge–Riemann relations); and Griffiths transversality ∇F^p ⊂ F^(p−1)⊗Ω¹_S.

items.name: Complex period domain and compact dual
items.statement: Let G be the semisimple Q-group acting on V_Q through which the variation's monodromy and Hodge structures factor (the derived Mumford–Tate group; see E27). D = G(R)^+·F_0 ≅ G/M is an open semialgebraic G(R)^+-orbit in its compact dual Ď = G(C)·F_0, a closed G(C)-orbit in a flag variety of V_C. Here M is compact but in general not maximal compact, so D need not be Hermitian symmetric. The G(C)-action on Ď is algebraic, and D has its complex structure and horizontal subbundle. For G = Aut(V_Q,Q) this is the full period domain with the given Hodge numbers.
proofSteps: Build the flag variety with the polarization isotropy relations and the open positivity locus.
Identify its points with the pinned PeriodDomain.Point carrier.
Construct the homogeneous complex structure and horizontal bundle; import the Hermitian specialization from ShimuraData.D2–D3 without claiming it covers every period domain.

items.name: Connected Hodge datum and canonical compact
items.statement: (Erratum §1.4) Let t : 𝐒¹ → 𝐆𝐋(V_ℝ) be the restricted Deligne torus of a pure polarizable ℚ-Hodge structure on V_ℚ and 𝐆 the ℚ-Zariski closure of t(𝐒¹) (connected reductive, with ℝ-anisotropic centre; in the original §1.3, 𝐆 is instead the adjoint group of the generic Mumford–Tate group). A component of the 𝐆(ℝ)-conjugacy class of t is identified with G/M, G = 𝐆(ℝ)⁺, M ⊂ G connected compact (the stabiliser of t). G has a canonical maximal compact subgroup K_t ⊃ M: the unitary group of the Hodge metric of the Hodge structure on 𝔤 induced by t. The Cartan involution θ_{K_t} of 𝔤 is the Weil operator of that Hodge structure.

items.name: Hodge morphisms preserve the canonical compact data
items.statement: For a rational Hodge morphism φ with φ∘t′=g t g⁻¹ and φΓ′⊂Γ, the induced map of Lie algebras is a Hodge morphism. It sends K_(t′) into gK_tg⁻¹ and its image is stable under the latter Cartan involution. The resulting map of pure Hodge manifolds is R_alg-definable.
proofSteps: Use functoriality of the Weil operator and the adjoint Hodge metric.
Verify both conditions of compatible-morphism and apply its definability theorem.

items.name: Finite buffered charts near a normal-crossing boundary
items.statement: Let S ⊂ S̄ be a smooth projective compactification with S̄ − S a (simple) normal crossing divisor. There are finitely many holomorphic charts φ_i defined on open neighbourhoods U_i' of the closures of open sets U_i ⊂ S̄, such that the U_i cover S̄, φ_i(U_i) = Δ^n and φ_i(U_i ∩ S) = (Δ*)^(r_i) × Δ^(n−r_i). Since each φ_i|U_i is restricted-analytic, the U_i ∩ S are R_an-definable open subsets of S. Φ_S is then R_an,exp-definable as soon as every Φ_S∘φ_i^(−1): (Δ*)^(r_i) × Δ^(n−r_i) → S_{Γ,G,M} is. Printed §4.1 asks only for a finite open cover biholomorphic to (Δ^n, (Δ*)^(r_i) × Δ^(l_i)) and does not say that the charts are definable.
proofSteps: Import characteristic-zero compactification and resolution with its exact boundary statement.
Use compactness to choose a finite buffered analytic cover.
Retain the smaller-disk restriction; holomorphic functions on an unbuffered open unit disk need not be definable near its outer boundary.

items.name: Quasi-unipotence of local monodromy
items.statement: The integral monodromy operators of a polarized variation around the coordinates of a punctured polydisk commute and have roots of unity as eigenvalues. Finite coordinate power covers make all of them unipotent.
proofSteps: Borel’s metric argument brings the conjugacy class arbitrarily close to a compact stabilizer, so eigenvalues have absolute value one.
Integrality and the same property for all conjugates allow Kronecker’s theorem.
Take a common multiple of the finite semisimple orders and pull back along power maps.
items.note: The lemma and proof were read; its horizontal metric-decrease input remains an original-source leaf.

items.name: Commuting nilpotent logarithms
items.statement: After the unipotent reduction, N_i = log T_i = Σ_(j≥1) (−1)^(j+1)(T_i−1)^j/j is a finite sum. It is a nilpotent element of the rational Lie algebra g_Q of G (T_i ∈ G(Q) is unipotent), and in particular a rational endomorphism of V_Q that infinitesimally preserves Q. The N_i commute (π_1((Δ*)^n) is abelian), and exp(N_i) = T_i.

items.name: Holomorphic extension of the untwisted map
items.statement: For a polarized variation on a punctured polydisk with unipotent monodromy, Ψ extends holomorphically to the full polydisk with values in Dcheck. Its limiting filtration F=Ψ(0) defines a nilpotent orbit. Auxiliary unpunctured variables are allowed on relatively compact subdisks.
proofSteps: Import the precisely stated nilpotent orbit theorem.
Use a smaller polydisk so the extension is analytic on a neighborhood of the closure needed for restricted analyticity.

items.name: Definability of the punctured-disk covering on a sector
items.statement: On a bounded real strip, z↦exp(2πiz) has R_an,exp-definable real and imaginary parts: e^(−2πy) times restricted sine and cosine in x. A finite set of overlapping strips covers the punctured disk of any fixed smaller radius.
proofSteps: Use real exponential for the radial factor and restricted analytic sine/cosine for bounded x.
Include angular seams with overlapping intervals; a single open strip 0<x<1 omits a radial ray.

items.name: Definability of the lifted local period map
items.statement: (Lemma 4.2.) Let V have unipotent monodromy on (Δ*)^n and let Φ̃: H^n → D = G/M be the lift of its period map. Then Φ̃ restricted to S_H^n = {0 < x_j < 1, y_j > 1} is R_an,exp-definable. More generally the same holds on {|x_j| ≤ R, y_j ≥ η} for any R, η > 0. The proof: Φ̃(z) = exp(Σ z_j N_j)·Ψ(p(z)), where Ψ: Δ^n → Ď is holomorphic on the whole open unit polydisk (Schmid (4.12)). The set p(S_H^n) lies in the compact polydisk |q_j| ≤ e^(−2π), on which Ψ is restricted analytic. exp(Σ z_j N_j) is polynomial in z, G(C) acts algebraically on Ď, and D ⊂ Ď is semialgebraic. No shrinking is needed.
proofSteps: Commutativity of the nilpotents gives a common finite polynomial exponential.
Compose the restricted analytic extension Ψ with the sector exponential, then use the algebraic action on Dcheck.
Restrict to the semialgebraic locus D.

items.name: Roughly polynomial function
items.statement: A real function f on Σ_n is roughly polynomial if f = g/h with g ∈ O[x,y,y^(−1)] and h roughly monomial. As printed (Definition 4.4, p. 929–930), h may be any roughly monomial element of O(x,y), and with that reading the class is not closed under addition (new sourceIssue). The repaired definition requires h ∈ O[x,y,y^(−1)] roughly monomial. That is what every use supplies: monomials, and the Gram determinants |B(γ w_det K^i)| ∈ O[x,y]. A complex function is roughly polynomial if its real and imaginary parts are, or equivalently if g ∈ O_C[x,y,y^(−1)] with h real.

items.name: Closure laws for rough functions
items.statement: Roughly monomial elements of O(x,y) are closed under products and reciprocals. With the repaired definition (denominators h ∈ O[x,y,y^(−1)] roughly monomial), roughly polynomial functions form a ring T_n and are stable under division by roughly monomial elements of O[x,y,y^(−1)]; the comparison constants are kept on the same sector. With the printed definition (h ∈ O(x,y)) the ring claim fails: for c = (x−1/2)² + y^(−2) and k = (c + y^(−1))/(c + 2y^(−1)) ∼ 1, both 1/k and −1 are roughly polynomial on Σ_1, but 1/k − 1 = y^(−1)/(c + y^(−1)) is not.
proofSteps: Multiply the two-sided bounds for monomials and use common nonvanishing denominators for sums.

items.name: Curve test for a global rough-polynomial bound
items.statement: For R ≥ 1 let Σ_n^R = {|Re z_i| < R, Im z_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ Im z_n > 1}; Σ_n is the part with 0 < Re z_i < 1. Let f be roughly polynomial and g roughly monomial on every Σ_n^R. Suppose that for every R, |f| ≤ C_{τ,R}|g| on every nonempty intersection of Σ_n^R with a complex affine curve α₁z₁+β₁=⋯=α_(n₀)z_(n₀)+β_(n₀), remaining coordinates fixed in H, for each 1≤n₀≤n, positive rational α_i and real β_i. Then one constant C bounds |f|/|g| on Σ_n. The R-uniform hypothesis repairs the printed proof (sourceIssues E2).
items.locator: Lemma 4.5, JAMS p. 930 (hypothesis strengthened to every Σ_n^R, following E2; the printed hypothesis concerns Σ_n only)
proofSteps: Clear roughly monomial denominators and reduce to g = 1 with f ∈ O[x, y, y⁻¹]. Expand f = Σ_j a_j x_1^{j_1} y_1^{j_2}. Taylor-expand the coefficients in t_1 = e(z_1): the terms that depend on t_1 are O(y_1^A e^{−2πy_1}), faster than every monomial, so the a_j may be taken independent of z_1.
Fixing the other variables along fixed-tail curves forces j_2 ≤ 0. Since y_1 ≥ y_2, it is then enough to bound |a_j| y_2^{j_2}.

For m ≥ 1 and c ∈ {0, …, r_1}, substitute z_1 = mz_2 + c. This maps Σ_{n−1}^{R′} into Σ_n^{mR′+c}, and affine curves of the lemma's shape to affine curves of the same shape (α_1 = 1, α_2 = m, β_2 = c). So f_{m,c} satisfies the hypothesis on every Σ_{n−1}^{R′}, and induction gives f_{m,c} ≪ 1 on Σ_{n−1}. The printed proof applies this with the hypothesis only on Σ_n, where the substituted sets are empty for c ≥ 1 (E2).

Use the normalized finite difference (−1)^r/r! Σ_(c=0)^r (−1)^c binom(r,c) f_(m,c), where r is the largest x₁-degree. It isolates Σ_j a_(r,j)m^j y₂^j. If the remaining exponents j lie in [−L,0], take L+1 distinct positive integers m; this is the ordinary Vandermonde matrix at 1/m for powers 0,…,L. Its inverse is constant, hence bounds each a_(r,j)y₂^j. Subtract those terms and descend in x₁-degree. The prior continuation's r₂+1 count was invalid when r₂<0; that was an extraction slip, not a printed-source error.

For the application in §4.5, establish curvewise bounds on every bounded real strip from the original Schmid and norm estimates. Theorem 1.5 is the conclusion, so its R-quantifier is not evidence for these inputs. G3 retains their unverified original-source uniformity.
items.note: Repaired by the continuation (Claude Code cc-fb70e5): the printed proof's substitutions leave Σ_n (E2). The R-uniform hypothesis makes the induction valid.

items.name: Constancy of monodromy weights on cone interiors
items.statement: For commuting nilpotents defining a polarized nilpotent orbit, every strictly positive combination of the nilpotents in a fixed nonempty face has the same centered monodromy weight filtration W(face). Faces with different sets of generators may have different filtrations.
proofSteps: Import the polarized nilpotent cone theorem with its positivity and face hypotheses.
items.note: Kashiwara’s statement was read; the original Cattani–Kaplan proof remains a gap.

items.name: Limiting mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: For F = Ψ(0) and N in the open cone C(I) = {Σ t_i N_i : t_i > 0}, (F, W(N)) is a mixed Hodge structure. With W(N) centred at 0, gr^(W(N))_j carries a pure Hodge structure of weight k + j (the actual weight filtration is W(N) shifted by k). N is a (−1,−1)-morphism, and S(u, N^j v) polarizes the primitive parts. The paper uses the induced MHS on g_R for N = M_n. Existence is a degeneration theorem.
items.locator: §4.4, JAMS p. 931; Kashiwara Theorem 2.3.2, p. 862 (= Schmid Theorem 6.16, p. 255, applied to the one-variable nilpotent orbit of N)
proofSteps: Use the polarized nilpotent orbit theorem and shift the centered weights to the actual Hodge weight.

items.name: Splittings adapted to all monodromy faces

The two splittings serve distinct purposes and are not identified.
items.locator: §4.4, JAMS p. 931; Kashiwara Lemma 2.4.1, p. 863 (distributivity) and Corollary 1.8.3, p. 860 (existence of the splitting)

items.name: Distributivity needed for simultaneous splittings
items.statement: For the limiting filtration F of a polarized nilpotent orbit and any nested sequence of nilpotent-generator subsets, F together with their monodromy weight filtrations is a distributive family and admits a common adapted splitting over C. The rational weight subfamily admits a rational splitting.
items.locator: Kashiwara Lemma 2.4.1, pp. 863–864, with Corollary 1.8.3, p. 860 (splitting); the rational splitting follows because distributivity descends from C to Q
proofSteps: Use the Cattani–Kaplan real-split replacement commuting with the nilpotents and inducing identity on the graded full weight filtration.
Induct on the number of nested faces; the two Hodge grading operators preserve the remaining weight filtrations.
Split the induced distributive subfamilies on each graded piece.
items.note: The selected proof was read; the real-split replacement and distributive-filtration algebra require exact supplier matching.

items.name: Asymptotic norm of a nonzero split flat vector
items.statement: Let V_C = ⊕_σ U_σ be any splitting adapted to all the W(M_j), that is W(M_j)_s = ⊕_(σ_j ≤ s) U_σ. Examples are the rational splitting J^σ ⊗ C and the complex splitting obtained by grouping the I^(p,q_1,…,q_n) with σ_j = p + q_j in the paper's centred labelling. For nonzero u ∈ U_σ, h_z(u,u) ∼ (y_1/y_2)^(σ_1)⋯(y_(n−1)/y_n)^(σ_(n−1)) y_n^(σ_n) on Σ_n. More generally h_z(u) ∼ Σ_σ (monomial_σ)·|u_σ|² for every u. This holds after rescaling the polydisk so that Kashiwara's threshold y_ν > M lies below Σ_n; otherwise one needs a compactness argument. Constants depend on the splitting and the variation.
items.locator: Theorem 4.8(1), JAMS p. 931; Kashiwara Theorem 3.4.1, p. 870, with Definition 1.9.3 and Corollary 1.9.2, pp. 860–861
proofSteps: Use the split-norm comparison theorem, with centered monodromy weights and squared Hodge norms.
Translate Kashiwara’s reversed variable order and logarithmic coordinates into this sector convention.
items.note: Kashiwara’s original p.870 was inspected as an image; the full proof and all its analytic inputs are not closed.

items.name: Asymptotic norm of a nilpotently twisted vector

proofSteps: Use the corresponding canonical-extension norm comparison, retaining the flat/untwisted frame conversion.

items.name: Holomorphic negative-Lie lift of the untwisted map
items.statement: For F=Ψ(0), the Deligne splitting of the limiting adjoint mixed Hodge structure gives a complement to the filtration stabilizer: the sum of pieces with first Hodge index p<0. On a sufficiently small polydisk there is a unique holomorphic v(q) in this complement, v(0)=0, with Ψ(q)=exp(v(q))F. Put g(q)=exp(v(q)) and γ(z)=exp(Σz_iN_i)g(q(z)).

items.name: Triangular form of the horizontal perturbation
items.statement: For negative-lie-chart, Griffiths transversality implies v(q)=Σ_i q_i v_i(q_i,…,q_n), with [N_j,v_i]=0 for j<i. Consequently g(q)=1+Σ_i q_i g_i(q), where g_i preserves every earlier monodromy filtration W(M_j), j<i.
proofSteps: Write the logarithmic derivative identity using the regular power series (1−exp(−ad v))/(ad v).
Compare the negative Hodge components and expand in the boundary coordinates successively.
Translate commutation with earlier nilpotents into preservation of their weight filtrations.
items.note: The source gives this implication briefly; the coefficient-recursion proof and its uniform holomorphic bounds remain explicit tasks.

items.name: Exponential decay against ordered-sector powers
items.statement: Fix integer exponents on y_i,…,y_n with y_i≥⋯≥y_n≥1. The product e^(−4πy_i) times any such Laurent monomial tends uniformly to zero as y_n→∞. Negative powers are bounded by one and positive powers by a fixed power of y_i.
items.locator: Lemma 4.10 proof, p. 932 ('For any monomial y^I only in y_i,…,y_n … |t_i|^2 y^I < ε for sufficiently large y_n')
proofSteps: Bound the monomial by y_i^A for a fixed nonnegative A.
Use exponential decay of e^(−4πt)t^A uniformly on t≥Y as Y→∞.

items.name: Comparison with the nilpotent-orbit frame
items.statement: Printed (Lemma 4.10): on Σ_n, h(γu) ∼ h(e^{z·N}u), i.e. h_z(γ(z)u) ∼ h_z(e^{z·N}u), where h_z is the Hodge form at Φ̃(z)=γ(z)F. The statement does not say what u is; the proof takes u ≠ 0 in J^{s_1,…,s_n}_C (the exponents of Theorem 4.8). Proven: there is Y_0 (depending on u) such that the comparison holds on Σ_n ∩ {y_n ≥ Y_0}, i.e. on Σ_n after shrinking the polydisk. Needed: Lemma 4.7(2) applies it to u ∈ I^α and to w_{det K^i} ∈ Λ^iV, which requires the version for nonzero u ∈ ∩_j W(M_j)_{s_j} ⊗ C with nonzero image in the multigraded quotient. Given Theorem 4.8 in that form, the same proof works.
proofSteps: Each q_i g_i preserves the earlier weights; apply the norm estimates to bound the error by the main monomial times e^(−4πy_i) and a monomial in the remaining variables.
Make the relative error norm smaller than a fixed number below one by increasing the minimum height.
Apply the triangle and reverse triangle inequalities for the positive Hodge norm.

items.name: Flag adapted to the Hodge filtration
items.statement: Choose an ordered basis w_i of the simultaneous complex splitting with decreasing first Hodge index p_i, and let K_i=span(w₁,…,w_i). The transported flag γK_i refines the varying Hodge filtration. Write B(u,v)=Q(u,conj v), which is generally indefinite. In pure weight k, B(v,u)=(−1)^k conjugate(B(u,v)); it is skew-Hermitian for odd k and i^kB is Hermitian.
items.locator: Lemma 4.7 proof, JAMS p. 931 (author copy p. 16)
items.note: E21 records the parity mislabel in the source. The determinant identities are sesquilinear, with the indicated phases.

api.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.refinesF
api.statement: The subflag at each Hodge-index cutoff equals that filtration step.

api.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.transportFlag
api.statement: γ maps K_i to the corresponding refined varying Hodge flag.

api.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.gramConvention
api.statement: B(u,v)=Q(u,conj v) is linear in the first variable and need not be positive definite. Its symmetry parity is (−1)^k, not uniformly Hermitian.

uses.how: Use Hodge-ordered subspaces for nondegenerate polarization Gram determinants.

unitTests.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.test1
unitTests.statement: A polarized two-step Hodge decomposition gives the prescribed ordered flag.

unitTests.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.test2

items.name: Nonvanishing of the adapted Gram minors
items.statement: For hodge-adapted-flag, B restricts nondegenerately to each γK_i. Its Gram determinant Δ_i=B(γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i),γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i)) is nonzero. Within each successive pure Hodge piece B has the scalar phase prescribed by the polarization.
proofSteps: Successively decompose along the orthogonal Hodge pieces.
On a fixed Hodge piece the appropriate phase multiple of B is positive definite, so refining the flag cannot introduce a degenerate restriction.
items.note: Ordinary positive-inner-product Gram–Schmidt cannot be applied directly to the indefinite form B.

items.name: Gram determinant and projection identities
items.statement: Let wtilde_i be B-orthogonalized γw_i along the adapted flag and set Δ₀=1. Then B(wtilde_i,wtilde_i)=Δ_i/Δ_(i−1). For any u, B(u,wtilde_i)=B(γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_(i−1))∧u,γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i))/Δ_(i−1). The analogous formula holds with γu.
proofSteps: Use determinant expansion for orthogonalized bases and exterior-power pairings.
All divisions are licensed by the preceding nonvanishing theorem.

items.name: Rational expression for all Hodge matrix entries
items.statement: In a fixed flat complex basis, every h_z(u,v) lies in the complexified fraction algebra O(x,y). Decompose u,v in the B-orthogonal adapted basis; its ith contribution is i^(2p_i−k) B(u,wtilde_i)B(wtilde_i,v)/B(wtilde_i,wtilde_i).
proofSteps: Entries of γ(z)=exp(zN)g(q) belong to the restricted-analytic polynomial algebra.
Apply the determinant/projection formulas, then the phase relation between B and the paper’s Hodge form.
Translate to the pinned conjugate-first convention only through the explicit conjugation comparison.

items.name: Rough monomial norm on a simultaneous Hodge-weight piece
items.statement: For a nonzero fixed vector u in a simultaneous complex piece I^(p,q₁,…,q_n), its squared Hodge norm is roughly monomial on a sufficiently deep ordered sector. The corresponding centered weight exponents are obtained by shifting p+q_j by the pure weight.
proofSteps: Compare the two adapted splittings using their common weight filtrations and a nonzero leading multigraded component.
Use the split norm asymptotics for two-sided monomial bounds, together with rationality of the entry.

items.name: Rough monomial norm of the transported vector
items.statement: For nonzero u in a simultaneous complex piece, the squared norm h_z(γ(z)u,γ(z)u) is roughly monomial, including the determinant vectors of the adapted flag in the induced exterior-power variations.
proofSteps: Use the same rational Gram expression for γu.
Combine twisted norm asymptotics with the relative perturbation comparison.
Apply the argument to the exterior-power Hodge structures used by the flag determinants.

items.name: Rough polynomial pairing of split vectors
items.statement: For u and v in simultaneous complex pieces, the real and imaginary parts of h_z(u,v) are roughly polynomial. Zero vectors give the zero function and require no roughly monomial assertion.
proofSteps: The absolute values of the adapted flag Gram determinants are roughly monomial.
Their signs/phases are fixed by the Hodge types; hence denominators can be expressed using nonvanishing rough monomials.
The numerator belongs to the polynomial coefficient algebra.

items.name: Rough polynomial Hodge form
items.statement: For any fixed u,v in the complex flat fibre, h_z(u,v) has roughly polynomial real and imaginary parts on an ordered sector after shrinking.
proofSteps: Expand u and v in the finite simultaneous splitting.
Use sesquilinearity and the ring closure laws.

items.name: Reduced positive form with an ordered basis
items.statement: Definition 4.11. Given an integral (ordered) basis e={e_i} of V_Z, a constant C>0 and a positive definite symmetric form b on V_R, b is (e,C)-reduced if (1) |b(e_i,e_j)| < C b(e_i) for all i,j; (2) b(e_i) < C b(e_j) for i<j; (3) ∏_i b(e_i) < C det(b). Here b(e_i)=b(e_i,e_i) and det(b) is the Gram determinant in e. [Extraction's extension, not in the paper: the same definition for ordered rational bases of V_Q. Rescaling each e_i by a positive integer d_i changes only the constants, by factors depending on the d_i. The Claim on p. 933 uses a rational basis.]

api.name: BKT.ReducedForm.offDiagonal
api.statement: Reducedness gives |b_ij|<C b_ii for every ordered pair.

api.name: BKT.ReducedForm.diagonalOrder
api.statement: For i<j, b_ii<C b_jj; this condition depends on the ordering of the basis.

api.name: BKT.ReducedForm.permutationRepair
api.statement: After obtaining uniform off-diagonal and determinant bounds, sort diagonal lengths; one of finitely many basis permutations then satisfies full reducedness with a suitable uniform constant.

uses.how: Separate off-diagonal bounds, ordering and determinant bounds before choosing finite permutations.

unitTests.name: BKT.ReducedForm.test1
unitTests.statement: For diag(1,T), T≥1, the standard order satisfies the diagonal condition with C>1.

unitTests.name: BKT.ReducedForm.test2
unitTests.statement: The reversed order fails that condition uniformly as T→∞ although product/determinant stays one.

unitTests.name: BKT.ReducedForm.test3
unitTests.statement: At C=1 strict inequalities exclude even the identity form; tests must use C>1.

items.name: Reduced forms and Siegel sets
items.statement: For an integral ordered basis e of V_Z and C>0, let T_{e,C} = {b ∈ X : b is (e,C)-reduced}. By classical reduction theory, every T_{e,C} is contained in a Siegel set of X, and every Siegel set of X is contained in T_{e,C} for some e and C>0 ([K90, Prop. 2, p. 18]). [Extraction's additions, true: T_{e,C} is semialgebraic, and the same holds for rational bases, since T_{ge,C} = g·T_{e,C} for g ∈ GL(V_Q).]
proofSteps: Translate Iwasawa coordinates into Gram matrix inequalities with determinant normalization.
Check changes from rational bases to integral lattices and the determinant convention.
items.note: The quoted original Klingen reduction proof remains a source-audit gap. Library support at the pins: Tau Ceti's TauCeti.cholesky and TauCeti.cholesky_mul_transpose give the decomposition b = NᵀDN behind reduced forms, and Mathlib's Matrix.inv_def the adjugate formula for (B⁻¹)_kk.

items.name: Basis change with determinant control and finite ordering
items.statement: Corrected form of the sentence on p. 933 (see E3). Let e and e′ be bases of V_ℚ, with m = dim V, and C, C′ ≥ 1. If b is (e′,C′)-reduced and ∏_i b(e_i,e_i) ≤ C·det(b in e), then there is C″, depending only on C, C′ and the change-of-basis matrix between e and e′, such that b is (σe, C″)-reduced for the ordering σ of e that sorts the values b(e_i,e_i); in particular b lies in the union of the m! sets T_{σe,C″}.
items.locator: §4.5, p. 933 (corrected form of the sentence 'Moreover, if b is (e′,C′)-reduced … (e,C″)-reduced'; see E3)
proofSteps: Apply basis-change-offdiagonal to obtain all-pairs bounds in e with K independent of b.
Choose a permutation σ sorting the finitely many diagonal lengths; positivity and C″>1 imply the strict ordering inequality required by Definition 4.11, even at ties.
Permutation changes neither the product of diagonal entries nor the determinant of the Gram matrix. C″>C supplies the strict determinant/product inequality.
The all-pairs off-diagonal bounds survive permutation and become strict because C″>K and all diagonal lengths are positive.
items.note: Not in the paper as stated: the paper asserts it for the fixed ordering e, which is false (E3). The proof needs two estimates the paper does not give. First: Let B be a positive-definite real symmetric n×n matrix, n≥1, d_k=B_kk, and D≥1 with ∏_k d_k≤D det B. For any real coordinate vector a and any k, aᵀBa≥a_k² d_k/D. Second: Let n≥1 and B be the Gram matrix in the ordered basis e′ of a positive-definite real form b. Suppose C′≥1, |B_ab|≤C′d_a for all a,b, d_a≤C′d_b for a<b, and ∏d_a≤C′det B, where d_a=B_aa. Let e_i=∑_a A_ai e′_a be another fixed real basis. Put k_i=max{a:A_ai≠0}, m_i=|A_(k_i),i| and L_i=∑_a|A_ai|. Then |b(e_i,e_j)|≤C′³ L_i L_j m_i⁻² b(e_i,e_i) for all i,j. The change matrix is fixed; the bound is uniform in b.
acceptance: The reversed basis of diag(1,T) is repaired by a permutation, never by an order-independent bound in the unreordered basis.
Rank one and equal-length ties require enlarging the constant above 1.
The change matrix may be rational or real but must be fixed as the form varies.

items.name: Bounded product of adapted diagonal norms
items.statement: Let e be a basis of V_Q with each e_i ∈ J^{σ_i}, σ_i=(s^i_1,…,s^i_n). Then on Σ_n, ∏_i h_z(e_i) ≪ 1, and det(h_z(e_i,e_j)) = |det Q(e_i,e_j)| is a positive constant. Hence condition (3) of Definition 4.11 holds for e with a fixed C. Reason: by Theorem 4.8(1), ∏_i h_z(e_i) ∼ ∏_j (y_j/y_{j+1})^{Σ_i s^i_j} (y_{n+1}:=1), and Σ_i s^i_j = 0 because W(M_j) is centred at 0. Also h_z = Q(C_z·,·) with det C_z = ±1.
proofSteps: Multiply the monomial norm bounds for the adapted basis.
Use the centered-weight sum zero on the determinant representation and the fixed polarization volume.
Keep any rational-basis determinant factor in the comparison constant.

items.name: One-variable period lift lies in a Siegel set
items.statement: For a unipotent local polarized period map and any R,η>0, its lift on {|Re z|≤R, Im z≥η} lies in one rational Siegel set for the compatible Hodge compact data.
items.locator: [Sc73, Cor. 5.29], cited in the paper at p. 921 (after Theorem 1.5, 'with |I| = 1') and p. 933 (proof of the Claim)
proofSteps: Use Schmid’s one-variable SL₂-orbit asymptotic factorization in horospherical coordinates.
Its positive-root coordinates tend to one or infinity and its other factors stay bounded.
Enlarge the set to include the remaining compact strip segment.
items.note: The corollary and immediate proof were read; the preceding SL₂ theorem is still an imported proof leaf.

items.name: Faithful representation compatible with the Hodge compact
items.statement: Choose a faithful rational polarized Hodge representation of the semisimple group used for D, possibly replacing the adjoint presentation by an appropriate central cover or by its adjoint representation. The induced map to the positive-form symmetric space has compatible maximal compacts and Cartan involutions; its preimage fibres include the compact K/M directions.
items.locator: §4.5, p. 932 ('The natural embedding G(Q) ⊂ SL(V_Q) defines a natural map ι : D → X'); extraction's adapter (see new issue on the adjoint G and E27); erratum §§1.4–1.5
proofSteps: Retain the group on which the chosen rational representation actually acts; an adjoint Mumford–Tate group need not act on the original standard lattice.
Construct the induced polarized variation and Hodge metric, and verify Cartan compatibility.
Compare the arithmetic quotient under any finite central change of presentation.
items.note: This is an explicit representation/central-cover adapter, not an assumed embedding of every adjoint Mumford–Tate group into GL of the original fibre.

items.name: Reducedness along each rational-slope curve
items.statement: Let τ be one of the curves in Lemma 4.5 (rational slopes α_i, remaining coordinates fixed). The pullback of the variation along τ, in the variable w/L with L clearing the denominators of the 1/α_i, is a one-variable variation with unipotent monodromy ∏_{j≤n_0} T_j^{L/α_j}. By Schmid [Sc73, Cor. 5.29] (Theorem 1.5 for n = 1) and Theorem 3.2, ι∘Φ̃(τ ∩ Σ_n) lies in finitely many Siegel sets of X, hence in finitely many T_{e'_k,C'_k}. Combined with condition (3) for the fixed J-adapted basis e, basis-change-offdiagonal then gives condition (1) for e along τ with a constant C_τ. Condition (2) holds only after a permutation.
proofSteps: Translate a rational-slope affine curve under q into a punctured-disk map with integer powers after a finite cover.
Apply the one-variable theorem and the corrected forward Siegel containment.
Use the determinant bound to transfer to the common basis; constants may depend on the curve.

items.name: Uniform reducedness up to finitely many basis permutations
items.statement: There are a basis e of V_Q with each e_i ∈ J^{σ_i} and a constant C such that, for all z ∈ Σ_n (after shrinking), h_z satisfies conditions (1) and (3) of Definition 4.11 with respect to e. Hence for each z, h_z is (σ_z e, C′)-reduced for any C′ > max(1,C), where σ_z sorts the h_z(e_i) increasingly. So ι∘Φ̃(Σ_n) ⊂ ∪_σ T_{σe,C′}, a union of at most n! reduced sets. [This is the corrected form of the printed Claim.]
items.locator: §4.5, Claim and its proof, p. 933 (corrected: finitely many orderings)
proofSteps: Apply the curve test to each matrix entry relative to the positive diagonal norm.
Take a maximum over finitely many pairs for one constant.
Use determinant control and the finite set of orderings; a single ordering on the entire sector is not asserted.

items.name: Finite Siegel containment for a local period lift
items.statement: Let a polarized integral variation on (Δ*)^n have unipotent monodromy and lift Φtilde:H^n→D. For each R,η>0 its image on H^n_(R,η) is contained in a finite union of rational Siegel sets of D, all for the canonical Hodge compact. The multivariable assertion is finite union, not one set.
items.locator: Theorem 1.5, p. 921; proof in §4.5, pp. 932–933. The Siegel sets are for the canonical Hodge compact, by the erratum's corrected Definition 2.5 (§1.1) and §1.4. Erratum §1.5 changes only the §4.5 citation and says the remaining introduction theorems are correct as written.
proofSteps: For each imaginary-order sector, use reducedness to cover the positive-form image by finitely many Siegel sets.
Use the corrected rational pullback theorem and the compact K/M fibre to obtain finitely many Siegel sets in D.

Extend the deep-sector argument to arbitrary positive η with finitely many buffered boundary-face charts and compact auxiliary parameters. The complement of a deep multivariable sector is not itself compact.
items.note: Uniform estimates with auxiliary parameters and the face-cover step remain an explicit proof interface.

items.name: Definability on a smaller punctured polydisk
items.statement: Let V be a polarized variation of pure Hodge structures of weight k on (Δ*)^n (Δ the unit disk) with period map Φ: (Δ*)^n → S_{Γ,G,M,K}. Then for every 0 < ρ < 1 the restriction of Φ to (Δ*_ρ)^n is R_an,exp-definable. The same holds for (Δ*_ρ)^r × Δ_ρ^(n−r), and definability descends through finite coordinate-power covers. The printed Theorem 4.1 claims ρ = 1, which is false (E1). The printed proof gives ρ = e^(−2π) (up to the rays arg q_j = 0; see the new §4.2 issue).
items.locator: Theorem 4.1, JAMS p. 928 (statement corrected per E1); proof §4.2, pp. 928–929
proofSteps: Work on finitely many overlapping bounded angular sectors over the smaller polydisk.
Compose the definable lift with the quotient map on the finite Siegel cover.
Descend through sector coverings and finite power covers; include trivial-monodromy coordinates by their analytic extension.
items.note: The printed whole-open-polydisk formulation is false (sourceIssues E1); see local-outer-boundary-obstruction.

items.name: Definability of the global period map
items.statement: Let V be a polarized variation of pure Z-Hodge structures of weight k over a smooth complex quasi-projective variety S. After replacing S by a finite étale cover (§1.3), let Φ_S: S → Hod^0(S,V) = S_{Γ,G,M} be its holomorphic period map, with Γ a torsion-free arithmetic group containing the monodromy. Give S the R_an,exp-structure extending the R_alg-structure of its algebraic structure. Give S_{Γ,G,M} the R_an,exp-structure extending the R_alg-structure of Theorem 1.1(1), taken, as the erratum requires (§§1.4–1.5), with respect to the canonical maximal compact K_t: the unitary group of the Hodge metric, whose Cartan involution is the Weil operator. Then Φ_S is R_an,exp-definable.
items.locator: Theorem 1.3, JAMS p. 920 (setting §1.3, p. 920); erratum §1.4 (canonical K_t) and §1.5 (p. 3)
proofSteps: Use a finite buffered cover of a normal-crossing compactification.
Apply the smaller-polydisk statement with compact auxiliary coordinates and finite étale level descent.
Glue the finitely many definable graphs.

items.name: Canonical structure on the symmetric space quotient
items.statement: Let X be the symmetric space of maximal compact subgroups of G; for every ℚ-parabolic 𝐏, 𝐏(ℝ) acts transitively on X by conjugation. For g ∈ G the natural map S_{Γ,G,K,K} → S_{Γ,G,gKg⁻¹,gKg⁻¹}, ΓhK ↦ ΓhKg⁻¹, is ℝ_alg-definable (by Remark 1.1(1)). Hence, identifying X equivariantly with (a finite quotient of) G/K by choosing a basepoint, Γ\X has a canonical ℝ_alg-definable structure. More generally, if Y is a G-space (continuous transitive left G-action with connected compact stabilisers, so Y ≃ G/M after choosing a basepoint), a choice of G-equivariant map Y → X gives Γ\Y an ℝ_alg-definable structure: a definable fundamental set for Y is the pullback of one for X.
proofSteps: Changing the base point changes K by conjugacy and the corresponding identification by right translation.
Apply the fixed-K/right-translation Siegel comparison; do not conclude that structures on a fixed Γ\G/M are independent of K.

items.name: Definable complex analytic Chow theorem
items.statement: Theorem 4.13 (Peterzil–Starchenko). Let S be a smooth complex algebraic manifold, which gives the C-analytic manifold S a canonical R_alg-definable manifold structure. Let W ⊂ S be a (closed) complex analytic subset that is also 𝒮-definable for some o-minimal structure 𝒮 expanding R_an. Then W is an algebraic subset of S.
items.locator: Theorem 4.13, §4.6, p. 933, cited as [PS09, Theor. 4.4 and Corollary 4.5]; used in the proofs of Theorem 4.12 (p. 933) and Theorem 1.6 (p. 934)
proofSteps: Import the Peterzil–Starchenko definable Chow theorem with the displayed hypotheses.
The original proof is a remaining prerequisite audit; projective analytic Chow alone does not provide this nonproper theorem.

items.name: A holomorphic map with algebraic graph is regular
items.statement: [Se56, Prop. 8] (GAGA). Let X and Y be complex algebraic varieties and f : X → Y a holomorphic map. If the graph of f is an algebraic subvariety of X × Y, then f is regular. (Proof in GAGA: the projection of the graph to X is a bijective regular map that is an analytic isomorphism, hence biregular by Prop. 9.)
items.locator: End of the proof of Theorem 4.12, p. 933: 'hence that f is algebraic (see [Se56, Prop. 8])'
proofSteps: Analytic graph projection is an isomorphism and has singleton fibres.
Establish the algebraic quasi-finite/birational comparison, then use normality of S and the absence of missing analytic points to identify the open immersion with S.
items.note: Precise algebraic/analytic comparison supplier and full proof still require decomposition; no properness of S is assumed.

items.name: Arithmetic and algebraic definability on Hermitian quotients
items.statement: ([KUY16, Theor. 1.9]; [PS13] for A_g) Let S_{Γ,G,K} be an arithmetic variety (G of Hermitian type, Γ torsion-free arithmetic), with the R_an-definable manifold structure induced by its complex algebraic Baily–Borel compactification. Then there is a semi-algebraic fundamental set F ⊂ G/K for Γ such that π|_F: F → S_{Γ,G,K} is R_an,exp-definable. Consequence (not written out in the paper): combined with Theorem 1.1(1), and provided F is contained in finitely many Siegel sets, the identity of S_{Γ,G,K} is an R_an,exp-definable isomorphism between the Theorem 1.1 structure and the algebraic (Baily–Borel) structure. The paper asserts more, without proof: the natural map S̄^BS → S̄^BB is R_an,exp-definable. Example 1.2 shows that it is not globally subanalytic, so the two R_an-structures differ.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 919 (paragraph after Theorem 1.1); Example 1.2, p. 920; needed, without citation, in the proof of Theorem 4.12, §4.6, p. 933; [KUY16, Theor. 1.9], [PS13]
proofSteps: Obtain definability of uniformization on a finite semialgebraic Siegel fundamental set in the algebraic target.
Use definable quotient descent to compare the two structures.
items.note: Acquire KUY16 proof and establish that its use here is independent of the Borel algebraicity theorem being reproved; do not silently identify the two structures.

items.name: Borel algebraicity via period-map definability
items.statement: Theorem 4.12 ([Bor72, Theor. 3.10]). Let S be a complex algebraic variety and let f : S → S_{Γ,G,K} be a complex analytic map to an arithmetic variety S_{Γ,G,K} (G of Hermitian type, K ⊂ G a maximal compact subgroup, Γ ⊂ G(Q)^+ a neat arithmetic subgroup, S_{Γ,G,K} with its complex algebraic structure, see §1.1 p. 917). Then f is algebraic.
items.locator: Theorem 4.12, §4.6, p. 933 (attributed to [Bor72, Theor. 3.10]; cf. Remark 1.4(2), p. 921)
proofSteps: On quasi-projective source opens realize the map through the homogeneous adjoint polarized variation; horizontality is automatic in the Hermitian case.
Use the algebraic-target structure comparison before applying definable Chow to the graph.
Convert the graph into a regular map and glue over the algebraic source.

items.name: Proper special Hodge subvarieties
items.statement: (Paper's definition) A special subvariety Y of the connected Hodge variety S_{Γ,G,M} is the image Y := f(S_{Γ',G',M'}) of some Hodge morphism f : S_{Γ',G',M'} → S_{Γ,G,M} (notions of [K17, §3.1]). The Hodge locus needs the strict ones, Y ≠ S_{Γ,G,M} (equivalently, image of a Hodge subdatum whose group maps to a proper subgroup of G). The printed definition includes the identity image (E28).
items.locator: §5, p. 933 (definition of special subvariety of S_{Γ,G,M}); strictness per E28 (§5, p. 934); special subvarieties of S are introduced in §1.4, p. 921

api.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.subdatumImage
api.statement: Form the image of the compatible arithmetic Hodge morphism at the chosen levels.

api.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.properGenericCondition
api.statement: The defining exceptional datum has strictly smaller generic Mumford–Tate group.

api.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.rationalTranslate
api.statement: Rational translates and connected arithmetic components are included in the same countable source family.

uses.how: Make the exceptional locus a countable collection of proper special images.

unitTests.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.test1
unitTests.statement: A proper extra-Hodge-tensor condition is admitted.

unitTests.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.test2
unitTests.statement: The identity morphism of the generic datum is excluded from the exceptional family.

unitTests.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.test3
unitTests.statement: The entire countable union is not automatically asserted definable.
